newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot natgas prices up in West due to outage.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot natgas prices up in West due to outage.

text.p: U.S. spot natgas prices were slightly higher in the West on Monday as the remainder of nomination deadlines for April 1 expired, sources said.

In west Texas, Permian basin prices climbed two cents to the high-$1.60s to low-$1.70s due to an unexpected outage at Pacific Gas and Electric's 1,073 megawatt (MW) Diablo Canyon 2 nuclear unit. The company said it would likely restart in a couple of days.
Helping to keep southern California border prices around $1.79-1.80 was news that the 1,070 MW San Onofre 2 nuclear unit in California had restarted over the weekend.
On Northern at Demarcation, where trading for next month finished this morning, prices were little changed from last week's levels in the low-$1.70s.
In the Gulf, swing April Louisiana Gulf prices were notionally flat in the low-to-mid $1.80s per mmBtu.

A blast of cold air in the Northeast pushed New York city-gate prices into the high-$2.20s, up about 10 cents, though trading was limited since many buyers chose to withdraw from storage to meet the short-lived heating demand.
In the Appalachian region, prices on Columbia were talked steady to lower at $2.02-2.07.
Weather forecasts are calling for normal to above-normal temperatures in the East and Midwest by midweek, while in the Southwest cooler weather was expected, Weather Services Corp said.
